skill.name: nestjs-code-audit
skill.description: Audit NestJS repositories for toolchain errors, boundary flaws, security risks, and runtime problems. Receive a prioritized report with evidence, remedies, and validation steps.
skill.summary: Review NestJS code quality with scoped evidence collection and a prioritized report of verified problems.
skill.author: amirtaherkhani

security_audit.summary: Most static findings match Markdown, JavaScript strings, or ordinary repository inspection rather than threats. Optional checks execute repository-controlled tooling and pass inherited environment variables, creating execution and credential exposure risks. No evidence found of intentional exfiltration or prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The optional check runner trusts local executable names without isolating binaries, ESLint configuration, or plugins.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit trust approval or sandbox checks without network access and with read-only repository mounts; inspect executable targets and ESLint configuration.

remediation.issue: Optional checks inherit all parent environment variables, including any available credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal environment allowlist and remove credentials and runtime injection variables before executing project tooling.

content.user_title: Audit NestJS Code with Evidence-Backed Findings
content.value_statement: NestJS repositories can hide boundary flaws and runtime risks that lint results alone cannot reveal. This skill combines local evidence collection and semantic review into one prioritized report.
actual_capabilities: Review full repositories or scoped paths across toolchain, architecture, design, runtime, security, and testing concerns.
Collect package metadata, Git state, TypeScript source inventory, and heuristic review candidates.
Optionally run installed local ESLint and TypeScript checks without fixing or emitting output files.
Trace imports, provider boundaries, request paths, authorization, and transaction ownership using bundled semantic guidance.
Deduplicate findings by root cause and assign severity, ownership, evidence, remedy, and validation steps.
Produce a Markdown report separating confirmed findings, missing evidence, healthy controls, and recommended remediation order.
limitations: Requires Node.js 20 or later and an existing NestJS repository; optional checks require installed local dependencies.
The collector does not run tests, builds, migrations, deployments, or dependency installation.
Source collection stops at 5,000 files, skips files larger than 1 MB, and treats heuristic signals as unconfirmed.
Read-only flags do not sandbox repository tooling; optional checks can execute project code with inherited environment variables.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Module
use_cases.description: Inspect a scoped module for dependency leaks, misplaced invariants, and missing boundary tests before changing its implementation.

use_cases.title: Assess Repository Readiness
use_cases.description: Review architecture, runtime controls, and available quality gates to prioritize repository improvements before a release.

use_cases.title: Inspect Authorization Boundaries
use_cases.description: Trace authentication, resource ownership, tenant isolation, and response handling while separating proven risks from missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Repository Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nestjs-code-audit to review this NestJS repository without changes or command execution. Report confirmed problems and checks that were not run.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Scoped Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit src/payments in architecture mode without running project tools. Trace consumers and transaction ownership; report evidence, impact, remedies, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Security Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit src/auth in security mode without live service checks. Trace guards, validation, tenant ownership, and output contracts; separate confirmed risks from verification needs.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Gates and Semantic Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full NestJS audit. Inspect local tooling and configuration first; run checks only after explicit approval in isolation with credentials removed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: combine controlled execution and semantic review.

output_examples.input: Review a payment module where a consumer bypasses the owning service.
output: Illustrative verdict: pass with risks for the reviewed payment scope.
Architecture finding: a consumer writes through an exported repository without enforcing the owning operation's invariant.
Minimal remedy: route the write through the owning operation.
Validation: add a boundary test proving the invariant remains enforced.

output_examples.input: Review a NestJS repository with missing local lint and TypeScript executables.
output: Quality gates: lint and TypeScript were not run because local executables were unavailable.
No dependencies were installed during the audit.
Semantic review remains separate from missing tool results.
Recommended next check: rerun gates after dependencies are available in an approved environment.

best_practices: Define the review scope and preserve existing changes before collecting evidence.
Inspect local binaries and configuration before checks; use isolation and remove credentials when executing project tooling.
Require file locations, call paths, impact, remedies, and validation for every confirmed finding.
anti_patterns: Treating a heuristic match, long file, or architectural preference as a confirmed defect.
Running untrusted project tooling because non-fixing flags appear safe.
Interpreting missing checks or clean lint output as proof of application security.

faq.question: Does this skill fix code?
faq.answer: No. It produces an audit report; implementation requires a separately authorized phase.

faq.question: Are specialist sibling skills required?
faq.answer: No. Bundled semantic references support standalone review; installed specialist skills can provide deeper guidance.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The bundled collector requires Node.js 20 or later.

faq.question: What happens when dependencies are missing?
faq.answer: Unavailable checks are marked not run. The audit does not install dependencies or treat missing checks as passes.

faq.question: Does a scoped audit limit every compiler check?
faq.answer: No. Source review and lint use the requested scope, while TypeScript checks the repository configuration as a whole.

faq.question: Are optional checks guaranteed to be read-only?
faq.answer: No. ESLint configuration, plugins, and local binaries can execute code. Inspect them and use isolation with credentials removed before running checks.
